answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation grow like a willow: slow, rooted, and hard to fake at scale. Each agent must earn standing through attested work over time, while saffron — rare and costly to produce — stands for the bond staked behind every identity, so creating a thousand fakes costs a thousand bonds. A trellis of peer attestations then supports only agents whose history checks out, letting honest newcomers climb gradually while fakes wither at the bottom with no yield.
